ATO_t = Sales_t / ((NOA_t + NOA_t-1)/2); the denominator uses a PLUS between current and lagged NOA. Average NOA must be positive. NOA = OperatingAssets - OperatingLiabilities; OperatingAssets = #6 - #1 - #32; OperatingLiabilities = #6 - (#9 + #34) - (#60 + #130) - #38. review_notes: Source-first scope decision: the principal question is H1, whether managers classify core expenses as special items. Table 6 / Equations (3a)–(3b) are the principal full-sample regressions: unexpected core earnings in year t and unexpected change in core earnings from t to t+1 are regressed on income-decreasing special items as a percentage of sales. These are distinct co-primary outcomes.

The primary design uses the All Compustat Firms column (76,901 firm-years). The nonzero-special-item and ≥5%-of-sales columns, serial-special-item Table 7, hand-collected Table 8, and analyst-benchmark/incentive follow-ups are outside the principal full-sample family.

Equations (1) and (2) are supporting construction regressions because their leave-one-out predicted values generate the two retained unexpected-core-earnings dependent variables. Each equation is one repeated industry-year specification; the model records preserve the reported varying fit counts and focal-firm exclusion rule.

Classification shifting is the substantive research question; the expected-core-earnings models are not treated as the paper’s principal method contribution. The supplied reading includes coordinator-verified math on pages 11 and 17; physical PDF pages 10, 11, 15, 17, and 18 were viewed. The ATO denominator uses the sum of current and lagged NOA, confirmed visually on pages 11 and 15.
